title: Why Don't We Live in an Art Nouveau World?
author: shcallaway
tldr: Art Nouveau faded within about 15 years because it depended on bespoke craft and star architects. Classicism, a codified style that ordinary builders could copy, replaced it. The author argues that modernism later won by pairing Art Nouveau's break with history with cheap industrial parts. The author thinks people resent modernism mostly because it is now everywhere.

keyPoints: At Barcelona's Sant Pau hospital, the most ornate Modernista pavilion housed the administration, not the patients.
After about half an hour at Sant Pau, the author found the ornament more tiring than restful.
In Barcelona, Riga and Nancy, architects left Art Nouveau within about 15 years for sober classical styles such as Catalan Noucentisme.
Classicism returned fast because its orders, parts and proportions formed a codified system that builders could learn from books.
Art Nouveau needed hand-made ornament and star architects, and that made it hard to build at the scale of a whole city.
The author argues that modernism is the scaled-up Art Nouveau, with the same architects, the same break with history, and standard industrial parts.
article.whyItMatters: Read the original if you follow the online argument that modern buildings are ugly and old ones were beautiful. It has the photos, the footnoted studies on how fast viewers tire of a building, and the career links from Art Nouveau architects to the Bauhaus.

comments.overview: A lively thread that mostly skipped the article's history and argued about why new buildings are plain. Cost was the main fight, with labor and maintenance on one side and priorities and incentives on the other. Several commenters named Art Nouveau towns the article missed, among them Helsinki, Oradea and Aalesund.

themes.title: Labor, maintenance and money
themes.synthesis: One camp said ornament died when skilled trade wages rose, and that flat facades are far easier to keep up. Others answered that poorer societies built cathedrals, so cost is a choice of priorities. A third group said modernist buildings often cost more over their life, because flat roofs and bare facades fail in rain and snow.

quotes.author: DubiousPusher
quotes.text: It is no coincidence that essentially every intricate form of architecture gave way to simplified forms at the exact same time that wages for trade workers were rapidly rising.

quotes.author: Yizahi
quotes.text: Funnily enough, all these constructivist and brutalist buildings are often in practice more expensive than something from 19th century.

themes.title: Houses as commodities
themes.synthesis: Many blamed developers and real estate portfolios that want identical boxes that are easy to resell or repurpose. Others doubted that plain houses really sell better and said grey paint is a choice nobody loves. One commenter who owned houses from the 1750s to the 1960s said ordinary houses never had much ornament anyway.

quotes.author: skinfaxi
quotes.text: Houses used to be built to be lived in, so ornamentation added value. Now they are commodities to be traded and sold, and variation makes a portfolio harder to manage/less uniform.

quotes.author: ninalanyon
quotes.text: I've lived and owned houses built from the 1750s to the 1960s in England and Norway and none of them have much in the way of ornamentation.

themes.title: What architecture schools teach
themes.synthesis: The top comment said today's architects cannot draw or sculpt and know little art history, and others blamed professors who sneer at classical styles. Some pushed back that the architects they know draw all day. One commenter said most architects work in the technical branch of the job. A former architect said the real limit is clients, since few have the budget for grand work.

quotes.author: lo_zamoyski
quotes.text: Talk to a dutiful architecture student and mention classical architecture, and don't be surprised if you get some eye-rolling or stock dismissals

quotes.author: Oarch
quotes.text: I was an architect. There's some truth to what you're saying, but to be honest we rarely get the chance to enact such grand visions. Normally the stars have to align with the perfect client who has limitless budget.

themes.title: Would a whole city of it be too much?
themes.synthesis: Some agreed with the author that a city of Sagrada Famílias would overwhelm. Others said you stop noticing, the same way people stop noticing mountains. The Sagrada Família itself split the thread, and a Belgian commenter called it grotesque and nothing like Horta's Brussels houses. Others warned that the surviving ornate buildings were homes of the rich, and that plain ones were forgotten.

quotes.author: ctolsen
quotes.text: I'm glad I don't live in a city where everything is like that. I feel like it'd be overstimulating much like an analog version of the Las Vegas strip.

quotes.author: Filligree
quotes.text: It’s no different from living in a beautiful natural landscape. I can tell you from experience that no, you get used to it.

themes.title: Style as politics
themes.synthesis: Some read the article's case against the trad critique as proof of it, since the author admits modernism spread as a cheap route to prestige. Others said taste in buildings has always marked political tribes. One example was Gothic against Italianate civic buildings in Victorian Britain.

quotes.author: vslira
quotes.text: at a point the author basically says that modernism has its hold due to being a (and I’m paraphrasing uncharitably here) cheap and easy shot at architectural respectability, which is not only not a defense of it, but pretty much the point of the “trad critique”

quotes.author: bonoboTP
quotes.text: The point is, architecture doesn't live in a vacuum, it is inextricably linked to political and ideological tribalism

comments.consensus: Most commenters agreed that new buildings are plainer than they want, and that money shapes this through labor costs, upkeep or developer incentives.
comments.dissent: A minority rejected the cost story and said cost is a matter of priorities, citing cathedrals built by poorer societies. Others said modernist buildings cost more to maintain than old ones.

contrarian.author: pfdietz
contrarian.text: I view them as social signals, something to indicate you can afford it, and that you belong in an elevated social class.
contrarian.why: Where most of the thread mourned lost ornament, this comment asks whether ornament was ever good for its own sake or mostly a display of class.
